subject: Audit & access log preservation — export windows & deletion controls
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <logs-team@finpay.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on retention window + bulk export format for audit/access logs

Hi Jasmine,

Quick intro: I’m Tom on FinPay’s infra/security team. We’re working through evidence collection for an upcoming audit and have a few questions about Redwood’s audit/access log retention and export capabilities. Can you confirm the following?

1) Retention windows: what are the default retention windows for hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)? Is there an option to extend to 12 or 24 months?

2) Export formats: for bulk exports, do you provide NDJSON/JSONL, CSV, and raw syslog output? Are token timestamps ISO-8601 with timezone?

3) Export mechanism: can exports be pushed to our S3 bucket (preferred) or do we have to pull from a signed temporary link? What are typical SLA/lead times for generating a 90-day export (~50GB)?

4) Deletion & legal hold: if we request deletion, what is the workflow and windows? Can we place a legal hold to prevent deletion while a compliance review is in flight?

We’d like a short plan we can share with auditors — sample commands or a runbook is ideal. Appreciate any attachments.

Thanks,
Tom
Logs Team — FinPay
logs-team@finpay.io

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <logs-team@finpay.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on retention window + bulk export format for audit/access logs

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear list, this is exactly the sort of detail auditors want. Short answers up front, followed by a few implementation notes and an attachment with the quickstart: 

- Retention by deployment: hosted = default 90 days (can purchase add-on for 12 months), Dedicated = configurable up to 24 months via reserved policy, Private (VPC/on-prem) = customer-managed (we provide the retention controls and playbook).

- Export formats & timestamps: exports are available in NDJSON (preferred for line-delimited records), CSV (for summaries) and raw syslog (for streaming). All timestamps use ISO-8601 with timezone offsets.

- Export mechanism & SLA: we support push to customer S3 buckets (preferred, secure with temporary credentials) and signed HTTP pulls. Typical generation time depends on size: a 50GB archive for audit logs is usually ready within 2–6 hours on Dedicated; hosted exports for larger windows may take 4–12 hours depending on queue/backfill.

- Deletion & legal hold: deletion requests are performed through the Console + signed request; there is a 48–72 hour safety window for hosted/Dedicated where deletions can be paused. We can place a compliance-level legal hold (no deletion) for active audits — requires an authorized request from your security contact. For Private deployments, deletion is under customer control.

I’ve attached a short quickstart (redwood_log_export_quickstart.pdf) showing the Console steps and the S3 push example; Markus (cc’d) will follow up with the low-level export playbook and NDJSON sample.

Next step: can you confirm the S3 bucket name + preferred timeframe (e.g., 2025-10-01 -> 2026-01-01) and whether you want the raw syslog stream or a point-in-time NDJSON snapshot? Once we have that I’ll open the export request and give an ETA.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on retention window + bulk export format for audit/access logs

Tom — adding the technical steps and a few caveats from the runtime side. Quoting the quick plan below so you can paste into your auditor packet.

--- Export runbook (summary) ---
1) Request: Create export request in Redwood Console -> Security -> Audit exports. Provide: timeframe (ISO), S3 bucket ARN, principal for upload (we give short-lived creds).

2) Preflight: We validate retention windows and legal-hold flags (if hold exists we will not DELETE). If you need a legal hold, email security@redwood.com with the authorized approver and ticket number.

3) Generation: For NDJSON snapshots we stream records into gzipped chunks (ndjson.gz) and sign them. Filenames include start/end timestamps. Each record is one event with fields: ts, src, actor_id, action, resource, request_id, meta. Example sample attached (export-playbook-ndjson-sample.json).

4) Delivery: We push to your S3 (recommended). We also provide a signed HTTP link valid for 72 hours. For very large exports (>250GB) we stage to our internal transfer nodes and notify you with multi-part upload instructions.

5) Post-export deletion workflow: If you request deletion after export, we document the export ID and sequence numbers, then apply deletion. Hosted/Dedicated have a 48–72 hour safety period; Private customers can execute immediate deletes but we advise retaining the exported archive until the audit closes.

Notes / caveats:
- Redaction: system-level PII redaction is opt-in per export. Request it explicitly if you need masking.
- Retention overrides require a signed amendment for hosted accounts (billing/SLAs).
- Timezones: all exported timestamps are normalized to UTC in an additional UTC-normalized column for ease of correlation.

If you’re happy with the plan, confirm S3 details and I’ll kick off the export job. I’ll also attach the NDJSON sample to the ticket for your auditor.

– Markus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
